title: Stretch: Planned Obsolescence and Cradle-to-Cradle
welcome_lead: Examine why products fail on purpose and how circular design rewrites the rules.

final_note: You can critique planned obsolescence and explain how circular design closes the loop.

concepts.def: Designing products to fail or feel outdated.
Designing so end-of-life feeds new products.

walkthroughs.body_html: Planned obsolescence takes many forms: physical (parts wear out quickly), software (older phones slow down) and stylistic (fashion seasons). It boosts sales but creates mountains of e-waste, and is increasingly resisted by right-to-repair laws.

Cradle-to-cradle design treats end-of-life materials as food for the next product. Bio-based materials return to nature as compost; technical materials are recovered cleanly and reused — keeping value in a circular economy.

The Fairphone is designed for disassembly with standard screws, modular parts and a ten-year support pledge. It directly opposes planned obsolescence and provides a material passport so recyclers know what is inside.
